rules.title: Newark Rent Control annual rent increase cap
rules.requirement: For covered housing spaces in Newark, annual rent increases at lease expiration or for periodic tenancies are capped at the CPI increase measured from 15 months before the proposed increase month to 3 months before it, with an absolute maximum of 4%. The cap applies no more than once in any consecutive 12-month period regardless of vacancy, tenant turnover, or ownership change, and no increase is allowed unless the dwelling is in substantial compliance and the landlord has met registration requirements.
rules.key_value: lesser of CPI increase or 4% once per 12 months

coverage_conditions.value: multiple dwellings / housing spaces subject to Chapter 19:2
coverage_conditions.text: Applies to housing spaces in multiple dwellings subject to Newark rent control.
coverage_conditions.quote: All multiple dwellings, as defined in subsection 19:2-2, are subject to Rent Control pursuant to this Title XIX Rent Control,

coverage_conditions.value: lease expiration or periodic tenancy increase
coverage_conditions.text: Applies when a landlord seeks an increase at lease expiration or for a periodic tenant.
coverage_conditions.quote: At the expiration of a lease or at the termination of the lease of a periodic tenant, no landlord may request or receive an increase greater than the percentage increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) from the CPI 15 months prior to the month of the proposed rent increase to the CPI three months prior to the month of the proposed rent increase.

exemptions.text: Hotel or motel space rented day-to-day to transients is exempt.
exemptions.quote: Any motel or hotel space rented on a day-to-day basis to transients;
Any dwelling, building or structure, or portion thereof, rented for commercial use;

exemptions.value: newly constructed multiple dwellings and vacant dwellings as set forth in § 19:2-18.1 and § 19:2-18.2
exemptions.text: Newly constructed multiple dwellings and vacant dwellings described in Chapter 19:2 are exempt.
exemptions.quote: Newly constructed multiple dwellings and vacant dwellings as set forth in this chapter at Subsections 19:2-18.1 and 19:2-18.2, respectively;

exemptions.value: federally/state rehabilitated units receiving Section 8 or federal vouchers during subsidy/program tenure
exemptions.text: Certain federally or state rehabilitated units receiving Section 8 subsidies or federal vouchers are exempt during the subsidy/program tenure.
exemptions.quote: Those units which have been rehabilitated by the Federal and State Rental Rehabilitation Programs as administered by the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development, the New Jersey Department of Community Affairs or the New Jersey Housing Mortgage Finance Agency and will be receiving Section 8 rent subsidies or Federal housing vouchers. In these units, rents will be allowed to be raised, but will not exceed the fair market rents as established by the United States Department of Housing and Urban Development. These units will be exempt only during the unit's tenure in the Section 8 subsidy or Rental Rehabilitation Program

exemptions.value: government-regulated rent contract that supersedes Newark authority
exemptions.text: Units under a governmental rent-regulation contract are exempt while that governmental agency's authority supersedes Newark's authority.
exemptions.quote: A contract between a landlord and a governmental agency duly providing for that governmental agency to regulate the amount of rent received by that landlord provided that, if the authority of that governmental agency supersedes the authority of the City of Newark to regulate such rents, then the application of this chapter shall be preempted during the period of governmental agency regulation specified in the contract.

rules.penalty: The landlord shall rebate to the tenant any amount of rent collected in excess of that permissible pursuant to the terms of this chapter by crediting the tenant with the amount of excess rent paid over a period not to exceed 14 months, or in the event the tenant is no longer in occupancy, by refunding within a one month period. The rebate to the tenant shall be retroactive to two years from the date of the petition.
rules.rule_quote: At the expiration of a lease or at the termination of the lease of a periodic tenant, no landlord may request or receive an increase greater than the percentage increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) from the CPI 15 months prior to the month of the proposed rent increase to the CPI three months prior to the month of the proposed rent increase. In no case shall the allowable rent increase exceed 4%.
rules.interaction_text: A contract between a landlord and a governmental agency duly providing for that governmental agency to regulate the amount of rent received by that landlord provided that, if the authority of that governmental agency supersedes the authority of the City of Newark to regulate such rents, then the application of this chapter shall be preempted during the period of governmental agency regulation specified in the contract. Until such a contract begins, and immediately after the contract terminates, this chapter shall continue to regulate such rents.

finding_note: The provided Newark city documents include the rent control ordinance (Chapter 19:2), administrative housing department provisions (Chapter 2:10), and Newark's housing/licensing ban-the-box ordinance (Chapter 2:31). None of the provided text enacts or proposes a Newark just-cause eviction law specifying allowable eviction causes, notice, relocation assistance, or coverage. Chapter 19:2 contains a policy statement mentioning fear of eviction and a heading for 'Retaliatory Eviction,' but no operative text for § 19:2-14 is provided in the documents, and no just-cause eviction standards appear in the supplied excerpts.

The provided Newark city documents do not contain a Newark-enacted or Newark-proposed security-deposit maximum or exception rule. Chapter 19:2 includes the term 'rent' to include 'security deposits and damage and cleaning deposits' in a definition, but it does not set a deposit cap or separate security-deposit amount rule in the supplied text. Other supplied chapters concern administration and criminal-record screening, not security-deposit limits.

Reviewed Newark city code excerpts provided (Rent Control Regulations; Department of Economic and Housing Development; Ban the Box Housing). These documents contain rent control, vacancy/property registration, and criminal-record screening timing/limits, but no Newark provision in the application_screening_fees category such as caps on rental application fees, permitted upfront screening charges, receipt/refund rules, or broker/finder fees charged to tenants.

rules.title: Ban the Box housing screening restrictions
rules.requirement: Landlords and real estate brokers may inquire into and consider an applicant's criminal history only after the applicant has submitted a formal application, must give specified written notice before any criminal history inquiry, and may not consider arrests not resulting in pending charges or conviction, expunged/nullified records, or sealed juvenile records. Newark also limits the lookback periods for most convictions, requires consideration of rehabilitation and related factors, bars ads referencing criminal history, and creates narrow exemptions where other laws require or permit such screening or where housing is designated for people with criminal histories.
rules.key_value: Criminal-history inquiry only after formal application; indictable convictions lookback 8 years, disorderly persons/municipal violations 5 years; certain serious offenses may be considered regardless of age

coverage_conditions.value: rental, lease, or sublease of real property
coverage_conditions.text: Applies to rentals, leases, and subleases of real property in Newark.
coverage_conditions.quote: In connection with any rental, lease, or sublease of real property,

exemptions.value: single apartment or flat in owner-occupied two-family dwelling
exemptions.text: Does not apply to rental of a single apartment or flat in an owner-occupied two-family dwelling.
exemptions.quote: the provisions of this Article shall not apply to the rental:1. of a single apartment or flat in a two family dwelling, the other occupancy unit of which is occupied by the owner as his/her residence or the household of his/her family at the time of such rental;

exemptions.value: room or rooms in owner-occupied one-family dwelling
exemptions.text: Does not apply to rental of room or rooms in an owner-occupied one-family dwelling.
exemptions.quote: 2. of a room or rooms to another person or persons by the owner or occupant of one-family dwelling occupied by him/her as his/her residence or the household of his/her family at the time of such rental.

exemptions.value: federal or state law requires or permits criminal-history consideration
exemptions.text: Exempt where federal or state law, regulation, or rule requires or permits criminal-history consideration, limited to those offenses and time periods.
exemptions.quote: Where any federal or state law, regulation, or rule requires or permits the consideration of an applicant's criminal history in the rental, lease, or sublease of real property, provided the exemption is limited to those offenses or types of offenses and time periods that federal or state law, regulation, or rule requires or permits the landlord or real estate broker to consider.

exemptions.value: property designated for government program encouraging housing for individuals with criminal histories
exemptions.text: Exempt for property designated to participate in a government program designed to encourage housing for individuals with criminal histories.
exemptions.quote: To any real property designated by the landlord or real estate broker to participate in a federal, state, or local government program or obligation that is designed to encourage the provision of housing for individuals with criminal histories.

rules.penalty: A first violation shall be subject to a fine of up to $500. Each subsequent violation shall be subject to a fine of up to $1,000.
rules.rule_quote: Inquiry into and consideration of any applicant's criminal history shall take place only after the applicant has submitted a formal application.
rules.interaction_text: Where any federal or state law, regulation, or rule requires or permits the consideration of an applicant's criminal history in the rental, lease, or sublease of real property, provided the exemption is limited to those offenses or types of offenses and time periods that federal or state law, regulation, or rule requires or permits the landlord or real estate broker to consider.

They do not contain any Newark ordinance, code section, or bill regulating algorithmic rent-setting software, prohibited algorithmic pricing conduct, or related penalties/effective dates.
